correctness.rationale: The centered H-description follows exactly from the symmetric cube matrix and constant cant perturbation and is independently restated in the 2024 follow-up. The source vertex formulas, after the centered translation, give \(R_k^2=k\ell^2/4+(d-k)(\ell/2-a)^2\), with increment \(a(\ell-a)>0\), so there are exactly \(d\) shells and the antipodal pole pair uniquely certifies the minimum enclosing sphere. For an inscribed ball, coordinate facets impose \(|z_i|+\rho\le\ell/2\) and difference facets impose \(|z_i-z_j|+\rho\sqrt2\le\ell-a\). These inequalities give the exact inradius and, at equality, force either \(z=0\) or \(z=t\mathbf1\) with the stated interval bound, proving the complete center phase.

value.rationale: Isocanted cubes are a named all-dimensional cubical-zonotope family introduced specifically as metric cants of a cube and later studied through volume and polar volume. The result gives a coherent metric profile rather than a single routine number: exact shell radii with binomial multiplicities, a cant-independent circumradius with a two-point contact set, and a sharp cant threshold where the optimal inscribed-ball center changes from unique to one-dimensional. The phase transition explains how the coordinate and root-system facet families exchange control of the inball.
